- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility bias; dampen forecast variance and favor mean-reversion patterns.
- True outcomes often show sharp downward corrections after high peaks; model fails to anticipate this; add a 3–5 day lagged low threshold trigger for downward adjustment.
- If true outcome includes multiple sharp drops (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 40), model should reduce forecast mean by 5–8% and increase volatility floor.
- Model underestimates true lows in 30-day horizon; adjust downward by 2–4% for periods with sustained low sentiment or policy-driven downward pressure.
- When sentiment history is static (all 0.00), model should not assume momentum; treat as “no sentiment” and apply conservative, symmetric mean-reversion correction.
